sn9.14:2.3: This is, of course, poetry. In the Vinaya, to be theft it must be something someone owns, and they must perceive it as taken and lost to them.
sn9.14:3.3: _Kena vaṇṇena_ is used occasionally in this sense ([sn10.2:3.1](), [thig13.4:2.3]()), which is apparently not attested in Sanskrit. The commentary explains _vaṇṇa_ here as “reason” (_kāraṇa_). In each context it appears in, there is an apparently hidden circumstance that needs to be brought to light. I think it anticipates the Pali _vaṇṇanā_ in the sense of “commentary”; cf. English “gloss”.
